name: Guar gum
short: Trials most often report abdominal pain, flatulence, diarrhoea and cramps. Case reports describe oesophageal and bowel obstruction from guar gum diet tablets; it can reduce absorption of medicines.
text: In a meta-analysis of randomised, placebo-controlled trials of guar gum for weight reduction, the adverse events most frequently reported were abdominal pain, flatulence, diarrhoea and cramps, and 11 patients (3%) dropped out because of adverse events; the authors concluded that guar gum is not efficacious for reducing body weight and that, considering the adverse events associated with its use, the risks of taking guar gum outweigh its benefits for weight reduction. An analysis of 26 case reports submitted to the United States regulator about a guar gum-containing diet tablet found 18 instances of oesophageal obstruction, seven of small bowel obstruction and one person reported to have died for whom too few details were provided to assess causation; half of those with oesophageal obstruction had pre-existing oesophageal or gastric disorders, one patient with oesophageal obstruction died from a complication of the procedure to remove it, and the authors noted that guar gum can swell 10- to 20-fold and may block the gut, especially when an anatomical predisposition exists. The abstract states that such products have been banned in Australia and that the tablet had recently been removed from the market in the United States. A review of herb-drug interactions states that soluble fibres, including guar gum and psyllium, can decrease the absorption of drugs.
